content.text:
I submitted index 10 (Cu 0.51 / Sb 0.49). It had the highest EQE of the three compositions I measured, but it only barely beat the runner-up. I used all 3 merit measurements and 4 of the 5 XRD scans.

**What I measured:**

| Index | Cu fraction | XRD | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21 | 0.19 | Mostly antimony oxide, several phases | not measured |
| 15 | 0.34 | Single phase, CuSb₂O₆-type | 0.00386 |
| 10 | 0.51 | CuSb₂O₆-type plus small traces of a copper-rich phase | **0.00394** |
| 7 | 0.60 | not measured | −0.0002 (effectively zero) |
| 5 | 0.66 | Several copper-rich phases | not measured |

**What the data suggests:** The active material is the CuSb₂O₆ phase, which covers roughly Cu 0.34–0.51. Activity drops to zero by Cu 0.60, where copper-rich phases take over.

**Caveats:**
- Index 10 beat index 15 by only about 2%, which may be within measurement noise. The two are effectively tied.
- With only 3 measurements, I tested two points inside the CuSb₂O₆ range, and the space between Cu 0.34 and 0.51 was not explored. I also skipped the region below Cu 0.34, where the antimony oxide phases take over. If the library's best composition is in either area, it was missed.
- The EQE values are very low in absolute terms (under 0.004%), so this library looks like a weak photoanode system overall under 2.4 eV light.
